Today you will take an excursion to the Hill of Seven Colors and the Humahuaca Gorge with a Russian-speaking guide, including national park entrance tickets and a stop in Purmamarca where you will leave the vehicle.
You will visit the world-famous Quebrada de Humahuaca, recognized by UNESCO for its cultural landscape, an extraordinary combination of magnificent scenery and a rich history going back more than 10,000 years. Here you will find the seven-colored hill of Sierra de los Siete Colores and the ancient Rosa de Lima church.
The route continues to Tilcara, where you will visit an ancient Indigenous fortress, and then to Uquía, whose church houses one of the most important collections of the celebrated “Ángeles Arcabuceros” (Arquebusier Angels). Humahuaca is situated on the banks of the Río Grande, where you can stroll along narrow old cobbled streets among monuments from the colonial era.
The excursion also visits Inca Cueva, a secluded high-altitude settlement in the puna with ancient petroglyphs and the traditional way of life of local communities.

Whale watching departing from the hotel – 45 minutes to 1 hour.

One of the most impressive spectacles nature has to offer is whale watching along Ecuador's Pacific coast, from June through September.

Every year, humpback whales travel about 7,000 miles from Antarctica, near the South Pole, to Ecuador's coast to mate. Here, they give birth to their calves and find conditions for survival in warmer waters.

Humpback whales can be seen in the ocean, around 30 minutes from shore, aboard motorboats approved by the Ministry of Tourism, accompanied by specialists who make the experience unforgettable.

RECOMMENDATIONS: comfortable clothing, sports shoes, a hat, sunglasses and sunscreen. During whale watching, you must follow the safety protocol explained by the instructors. Whale sightings depend on weather and sea conditions.

IMPORTANT: This excursion is not recommended for pregnant women, people with spinal problems or anyone who has recently undergone surgery. The guide reserves the right to refuse participation to anyone who does not meet these requirements or is under the influence of alcohol or drugs, without a refund.

From Foz do Iguaçu, the group crosses into Argentina on the Tancredo Neves Bridge over the Iguazú River. On this side of the falls, paths and walkways pass above the cascades and close to the plunging water.

A Russian-speaking guide accompanies the walk through the nature park. The viewing platforms bring you close to the torrents and offer views of the Devil's Throat, where a dense cloud of spray rises above the falls. After the broad panoramas from the Brazilian bank, the proximity of the water is especially striking.

The excursion is included in the tour's group program. Afterwards, a transfer to the airport is arranged for the flight to Buenos Aires.
